candidates: When an e2e test or test-infrastructure script reads a required environment variable whose absence should be a hard failure, do not suppress the TypeScript error with a non-null assertion (`!`). Instead, read the raw value and add an explicit runtime guard that throws a descriptive `Error` naming the variable, explaining why it is required, and—where a known default exists—pointing to it (e.g. sandboxes are generated outside the repo at `../storybook-sandboxes/`). This ensures CI and local-dev failures are immediately actionable rather than producing a cryptic downstream crash.
